requirement: `message` sets the task-specific text at the beginning of the opening user message, before queued node contents. The last call supplies the text. The system prefix and its fingerprint depend only on `context` calls.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.subject_message` states only observable behavior, so it has no structural obligation. The clauses are: (1) `message` "sets the task-specific text at the beginning of the opening user message, before queued node contents"; (2) "The last call supplies the text"; (3) "The system prefix and its fingerprint depend only on `context` calls". Clause 1 is about message ordering. Clause 2 is last-write-wins. Clause 3 is about which inputs affect the prefix and fingerprint. The text names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field or delegation interface. An implementation could store the message in a field, a list or a builder, and could compute the prefix and fingerprint in any module. It would still conform if it produced the same message ordering, the same last-call-wins result and the same prefix and fingerprint dependence. Those choices are discretionary. The review roots are empty and there are no implementation edges. Since no structural obligation needs implementation evidence, no root is missing. The behavioral obligations are for the behavioral test criterion to assess.

behavioral: Obligations: (1) the `message` text sits at the start of the opening user message, before queued node contents; (2) the last `message` call supplies the text; (3) the system prefix and its fingerprint depend only on `context` calls.

- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/configured.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_late_task_message_precedes_the_first_source_in_the_provider_request]` covers (1) and (2) end to end. It calls `.message("old task")`, then `.contents_of_current_node()`, then `.message("new task")`. It reads the provider request's user message. It asserts that the message starts with "new task", that it contains the source snapshot, and that it does not contain "old task".
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs#fn[task_messages_share_a_prefix_and_can_queue_another_node]` covers (2) and (3). Each call sets a "superseded" message and then a final task, "assess" or "verify". The test asserts that the agent received exactly ["assess","verify"], so the last call wins. For both requests it asserts that the prefix is "shared" and that the fingerprint equals `context_fingerprint("shared")`. The messages differ between the two requests, so the prefix and fingerprint do not depend on `message`. It also asserts that the node inputs are queued separately from the message.
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[citation_reviews_use_their_prompt_and_record_the_item_and_citations]` adds supporting evidence. It asserts that the user message starts with the task text ("# Subject\n\nItem under review:") and that the source contents come after the task text.

I found no untested obligation. The configured-provider test does not assert on the system message directly. The graph-level test covers the prefix and fingerprint independence, and that is the behavior the requirement states.
